extracted.intended_audience: novelists and serious fiction writers studying point-of-view and dramatization
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to present a character's inner life and gradual moral/intellectual change by controlling point of view, withholding authorial exposition, and dramatizing surface impressions rather than summarizing inner states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view aligned with central change
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a story which must obviously be told from Strether’s point of view... The change in his purpose is due to a change in his vision, and the long slow process could not be followed unless his vision were shared by the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the heart of the subject is a character's internal change, choose a focaliser whose consciousness can carry that slow alteration to the reader; the reader must share the character's vision to understand the transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict narration to the character's impressions (pictorial subject)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a purely pictorial subject, covering Strether’s field of vision and bounded by its limits; it consists entirely of an impression received by a certain man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the narrative world to what the focal character perceives and interprets; render setting, people, and events as elements of that character's impressions rather than as independent, omniscient descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the external dramatic method for internal subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The dramatic method, as we ordinarily understand it, is ruled out at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject is primarily interior or pictorial, do not attempt to treat it as external dramatic action (pure stage-like presentation); instead, dramatize the inner life through carefully controlled impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show thought by surface enactment, not retrospective account
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere account of its working, after the fact, has already been barred; we have found that this of necessity is lacking in force, it is statement where we look for demonstration... the author must so arrange matters that Strether’s thought will all be made intelligible by a direct view of its surface. The immediate flaw or ripple of the moment, and the next and the next, will then take up the tale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate a mind's processes by presenting its momentary images, ripples, gestures, and speech-sequences rather than summarizing or explaining the internal working after the fact; use successive surface moments to dramatize mental change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refrain from authorial intrusion and privileged exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Henry James knows all there is to know of Strether, but he most carefully refrains from using his knowledge. He wishes us to accept nothing from him, on authority — only to watch and learn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid telling the reader what to think via narrator commentary or supplying facts the focaliser does not possess; let readers infer from what they are shown rather than relying on authorial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not allow the narrator to disclose privileged knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose him to begin sharing the knowledge that he alone possesses... he must at once give us the whole of it, must let us into every secret without delay, or his exposition is plainly misleading. It is assumed that he tells all, if he once begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you begin to operate as an omniscient commentator, you are committed to full disclosure and risk undermining suspense and dramatic effect; preserve the constraints of your chosen focalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dramatic devices (delay, suspension, restraint) within close focalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The story in it is played out by due degrees, and there may be just as much deliberation, refrainment, suspension, as in a story told scenically upon the stage. All the effect of true drama is thus at the disposal of the author, even when he seems to be describing and picturing the consciousness of one of his characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when using close, impressionistic point of view, employ dramatic timing—delaying revelation, withholding explanations, and creating suspense—so that the effects of drama are available without breaking the method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show gradual internal change through multiple small scenes and glimpses
rubrics_metrics.description: To bring his mind into view at the different moments, one after another, when it is brushed by new experience — to make a little scene of it, without breaking into hidden depths where the change of purpose is proceeding — to multiply these glimpses until the silent change is apparent, though no word has actually been said of it: this is Henry James’s way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map an internal transformation by a series of scenes, impressions, and minor moments rather than a summary statement; accumulate evidence until the reader perceives the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame other characters only as they appear to the focaliser
rubrics_metrics.description: All the other people in the book face towards him, and it is that aspect of them, and that only, which is shown to the reader; still more important, the beautiful picture of Paris... is Strether’s picture, his vision, rendered as the time and the place strike upon his senses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working in a single-character focalization, render other characters and the world as they are seen and interpreted by that focaliser; do not provide independent portraits that contradict the focal perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate objective dramatic presentation and interior access while preserving focal framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Simply it consists in treating the scene as dramatically as possible — keeping it framed in Strether’s vision, certainly, but keeping his consciousness out of sight, his thought unexplored... He talks to Maria; and to us, to the reader, his voice seems as much as hers to belong to somebody whom we are watching — which is impossible, because our point of view is his.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may sometimes step back from interior commentary during dialogue or scene to allow characters' speech and action to function objectively, but always keep the scene presented within the visual/interpretive bounds of the focaliser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply dramatic arts to pictorial/undramatic subjects (animate description)
rubrics_metrics.description: The less dramatic, strictly speaking, the subject may be — the less it is able... to express itself in action and in action only — the more it is needful to heighten its flat, pictorial, descriptive surface by the arts of drama. It is not managed by peppering the surface with animated dialogue... The dramatic rule is applied more fundamentally; it animates the actual elements of the picture, the description, and makes a drama of these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When subject matter is inherently 'pictorial' or static, don't fake drama with unnecessary talk; instead, animate description itself—turn descriptions into enacted moments, give images dynamic dramatic weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveal central facts by surrounding and implying them, not by direct statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Not to walk straight up to the fact and put it into phrases, but to surround the fact, and so to detach it inviolate — such is Henry James’s manner of dramatizing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encircle a withheld truth by related images and small clues; let the fact 'spring up' in the reader's mind through implication rather than explicit announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent deep motives through their outward manifestations
rubrics_metrics.description: By no picture of them but by an enactment of their remotest manifestations — that is how their strength, their bulk, their range in a harassed existence is represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of describing inner drives directly, show their effects—the tiny gestures, halting phrases, looks, and behaviors that manifest deep motives; these enacted signs communicate depth without exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dramatization to create solidity, weight, and three-dimensional character
rubrics_metrics.description: Solidity, weight, a third dimension, is given to the impression of Milly’s unhappy case... just as with two eyes, stereoscopically, we shape and solidify the flat impression of a sphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ multiple angled glimpses, subtle variations of scene and moment, and enactments of surface impressions to build a sense of character's fullness and material presence rather than leaving them flatly described.
